parsed.why: No trans-specific offence or documented targeting; the 2019 Gender Equality Act bars gender-identity discrimination and mandates official sensitisation. Absence of trans-violence or border friction in a documented state is mildly positive; no active visitor restriction.

Same-sex conduct remains criminally enforced and public-morality policing targets gender-nonconforming people; the 2022 cross-dressing ruling did not end official discrimination or dress-code harassment. The ombudsman records trans-only targeting, with no working recourse.

No criminalisation of trans identity, but very low acceptance, documented LGBT torture/extortion/violence, legislators' death threats against a trans woman, and slow or absent police response; hate-crime protection is ambiguous. Social hostility with thin recourse.

Sodomy was repealed and the 2024 hate-crime law expressly covers gender identity with enhanced penalties; no documented trans-specific border, facilities, police, or violence exposure. Strong statutory recourse, though social practice is undocumented.

No criminalisation and hate-speech and hate-crime laws exist, but gender identity is absent from general equal-treatment grounds and enforcement is inconsistent; clergy incitement and anti-gay attacks drew little police action. Partial protections, uneven recourse.
